blocks.text: Acute respiratory failure (ARF) is a life-threatening condition in which the respiratory system fails to maintain adequate oxygenation, adequate carbon dioxide elimination, or both, resulting in impaired gas exchange.
It is generally identified by abnormalities in arterial blood gases (ABG), interpreted alongside the patient's clinical condition.

items.text: PaO₂ below 60 mmHg (8 kPa), indicating significant hypoxaemia.
PaCO₂ above 45–50 mmHg (6–6.7 kPa), indicating hypercapnia, particularly when associated with respiratory acidosis.

blocks.text: The presence of respiratory failure does not automatically mean that the patient requires intubation. Management depends on the underlying mechanism, severity, response to initial treatment and ability to maintain airway protection.
There are two principal types.
